title: Audit the 20-prefix confinement step of the length-22 exclusion (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and scope

**Bounded independent verification; no kappa, no selected-frontier change.** Adds `research/f7-l22-confinement-audit/`.

PR #3058 proves `f(7) = 24` in PR943's singleton prefix-walk model. Its length-22 argument rests on `|P| >= 20` (published covering bound), then on excluding `|P| = 20`, `21` and `22`. This PR audits the **`|P| = 20` step** with its own code and its own derivation.

**Argument re-derived here.** If `|P| = 20`, every position of the walk lies in the twenty-point set `T = P`, so the walk is a closed walk spanning `T` and the graph induced on `T` by the walk's seven directions must be connected. Each basis direction contributes only the pairs of `T` at one difference, so

```
edges <= sum of the seven largest multiplicity classes of diff(T),
```

while a graph on twenty vertices with at most two components needs at least eighteen edges. Every 20-point cover is an affine image of `{0} u S` for one of the five 19-point representatives in DMP's Table 1 (imported), and `G(M T + b, D) = G(T, M^-1 D)`, so one inequality per representative covers every basis and every cover.

| Representative | seven largest multiplicities | sum | edges needed | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1, 2, 3 | 3,3,3,3,3,3,3 | 21 | 18 | arithmetic insufficient |
| 4, 5 | 2,2,2,2,2,2,2 | **14** | 18 | **excluded for every basis, by arithmetic** |

Representatives 1-3 are reported **open** with bounded evidence only: exact canonical-basis component counts 9, 12, 4 and deterministic 200-base sample minima 6, 5, 5. No sampled basis produced two components. Sampling is not a proof and the package says so.

Also re-derived: a simple 22-cycle can only carry the multiplicity patterns `(6,4,4,2,2,2,2)` and `(4,4,4,4,2,2,2)`, from the imported projections `f(6) = 16` and `f(5) = 12`. Word-level searches give a **universal 24-step positive control** (`145164232614626031626540`, 128/128, `|P| = 24`, restored) and two non-universal simple 22-cycles as controls: `1206231531046325014203` at 126/128 (pattern B, masks 82 and 120 unrealised) and `2130240236105010621045` at 125/128 (pattern A).

## What this does not establish

Not a re-proof of `f(7) = 24`. The covering bound, the cover classification, `f(5) = 12`, `f(6) = 16`, the size-21 argument and the size-22 exhaustion are imported. Three of five cover classes remain sampled. No census, no tariff, no supplier, no kappa.

## Validation

- `python3.12 -B research/f7-l22-confinement-audit/verify.py` -> `PASS_F7_L22_CONFINEMENT_AUDIT arithmetic_complete=2/5 sampled_only=3 f7_untouched` (well under a second, stdlib only, deterministic).
- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-l22-confinement-audit` -> `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.
- `python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/f7-l22-confinement-audit --check-source-history` -> `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.
- Interpreter: `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12` (CPython 3.12), `git rev-parse HEAD` = `0f000bb4aac86fa667906d8092eb36e49a76944a`, base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`.
- `scripts/research_baseline.py` could not run in this sparse checkout (it reads a selected-record file that is not materialised); that is a checkout artifact, not a result.

Overlap: `python3 scripts/find_overlap.py --task census-pruning-audit` was run before submission; its report states its own coverage and freshness.
